items.title: fix(dns): make save.sh encrypt tfstate atomically (#6536)
items.body: Fixes #6536. save.sh now encrypts to a temp file in the same directory, verifies it is non-empty and decrypts back to exactly the plaintext state (which also proves lineage, mirroring plan.sh), preserves the existing .enc mode, and atomically renames it over terraform.tfstate.enc. A failed or interrupted sops run leaves the previous .enc byte-identical; the EXIT trap removes the temp file and the .lock exactly as before. Adds infra/dns/test_save_atomic.sh (stub identity-cipher sops; oracle: the previous .enc is the record): failing -e leaves .enc unchanged with non-zero exit and no temp/lock residue, succeeding -e installs the new ciphertext, already-current fast path still skips re-encryption - 9/9 checks pass on the laptop. load.sh assessment (recorded on #6536): its in-place decrypt write is safe-by-reconstruction - the plaintext target is fully re-derivable from the intact .enc, so a truncated plaintext is recovered by re-running load; it is documented rather than changed. Shellcheck reports only pre-existing style findings for save.sh. Queue task 14343, lane code-h. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(talos): save-secrets.sh encrypts atomically and fails loudly (#6554)
items.body: Fixes #6554. **Defect (verified at current main):** `infra/talos/01b.us/save-secrets.sh` redirected `sops --encrypt` straight into `secrets.enc`, so the shell truncated the sole encrypted copy before sops ran; with no `set -e`, a failed encryption left `secrets.enc` at 0 bytes while the script exited 0 (reproduced with a stub sops exiting 1: exit 0, 25 bytes -> 0 bytes, md5-identical script). **Fix:** - `set -Eeuo pipefail` (house style) so tar/sops failures exit non-zero and `init-talos.sh` stops. - Encrypt to same-directory `mktemp` files; `mv` over `secrets.enc` only after sops exits 0 **and** the temp ciphertext is non-empty. - `EXIT` trap removes plaintext/ciphertext temps (plus stale legacy `secrets.tmp`) without touching the live `secrets.enc`. **Probes (stub sops, /tmp):** - failing sops: exit 1, `secrets.enc` sha256-identical, no leftover temps, stale `secrets.tmp` cleaned. - succeeding stub: exit 0, new ciphertext in place, no leftover temps. - sops exits 0 but writes nothing: exit 1, `secrets.enc` unchanged. - `load-secrets.sh` round-trip of a saved artifact extracts byte-identical `secrets/`. - `shellcheck --severity=warning` clean; `shfmt -d` clean. Out of scope: #6536 (dns/save.sh counterpart), `load-secrets.sh` hardening. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(id): durable replication receiver + verifier (#806 phase 3)
items.body:
## Phase 3 of #806 (F12.13): durable receiver + verifier

Implements phase 3 of the phased plan in `doc/2026-11-01_design_id806.md` §7, on top of phase 1 (PR #4447, wire contract + `ReplicationTracker`) and phase 2 (PR #4589, writer snapshot-plus-subscribe feed; merged as 51535c2b, this branch's base).

### What lands

New module `pkgs/id/src/world/replication_receiver.rs`: `DurableReceiver`, a durable replica of one world's journal from one pinned source.

- **Pinned-source verification** — every frame goes through the phase-1 `ReplicationTracker` built with the receiver's pinned source; untrusted signers, bad signatures, nonce replays, gaps, forks, stale replays, unsupported journal versions, and oversized payloads are refused by the tracker before payload staging.
- **Staged transfers** — accepted snapshot/tail payloads are staged in memory only. Nothing becomes durable until the batch's signed terminal frame verifies (§4.4/§4.5): truncated, refused, or disconnect-abandoned transfers leave the last committed replica untouched. A staged-transfer size bound (64 MiB) keeps an unterminated stream from growing memory without limit; exceeding it poisons the session rather than desynchronising staging from verification.
- **Atomic snapshot install, append-only tails** — a committed snapshot is written to a scratch file, fsynced, renamed over `journal.jsonl`, and the directory is fsynced, so a crash mid-install never leaves a torn journal (a leftover scratch file is cleaned up at open). Committed tail batches append + fsync; committed bytes are never rewritten.
- **Restart / reconnect** — `DurableReceiver::open` re-reads the committed journal, refuses it if it is not a well-formed chain for this world at a supported header version (decodable lines, exactly one leading `Created` header), and recomputes the verified cursor from the entry bytes under the pinned source. Every session opens with a snapshot (the phase-2 feed contract), which rebases the tracker; staged bytes from a dead session are discarded.

### Scope note — module transfer

The packet scope mentions module transfer/hash checks. The phase-1/2 contract as built carries journal bytes only — there is no module-bytes frame kind in v1, so there is no module payload for the receiver to hash-check. Module hashes named by journal entries (e.g. `BuilderInstalled.module_hash`) are covered by the cursor chain like every other entry byte. This is recorded in the module docs; adding a module frame kind is a wire-contract change for a later phase, not something phase 3 can invent receiver-side.

### Tests

13 tests in the module (`cargo test --lib replication_receiver`): snapshot commits only on terminal; truncated/abandoned transfer commits nothing; tail batch withholds append until its terminal, then appends exactly; tampered payload refused with committed replica intact; untrusted source refused; gap and fork tails refused; unsupported journal version refused before any entry; oversized payload refused (signed through a test-only unbounded path, per Codex); captured frames replayed into a new-nonce session refused; reset snapshot replaces the journal and bumps the header version; restart reopens committed state and a corrupt journal is refused at open; frames without a session are refused; a session starting with a tail or terminal is refused before the tracker sees it; an interrupted tail append (torn or entry-boundary debris under a durable append-pending record) is rolled back at open.

Refs #806 (phase 3 of 5; #806 closes when phase 5 lands). Queue task 6536.
